translations.answer: The original author confirmed that the floating base velocity, quaternion propagation, and integrator were processed in global coordinates, which is incompatible with the free-flyer local velocity required by the Pinocchio Jacobian. Alignment of local expressions yielded the expected result. The finite difference application q_plus = pin.integrate(model, q, v * eps) was performed on the configuration manifold, and the frame world position difference was used for comparison; the C++ output Jacobian should verify J is zeroed in advance.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the frame Jacobian of Pinocchio floating base model and numerical differentiation validation; the original post does not specify the version or specific robot.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The project contributor provided a minimal Python code for the finite difference of pin.integrate and the frame velocity, Jv.
translations.details.attempts.1: There was an error in the explanation of getFrameVelocity during discussion, which was later corrected by the original reply; this card does not use the previously corrected old explanation.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Constructed the local configuration on the manifold using q_plus = pin.integrate(model, q, v * eps), and compared with the frame world position difference.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Verify that the free-flyer base twist is provided in the local coordinate system as per Pinocchio, and do not directly pass global coordinate velocities.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Ensure that J is zeroed in advance when using the output parameter in the C++ getFrameJacobian function.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Align the floating base velocity, quaternion propagation, and integrator with the free-flyer local velocity required by Pinocchio; use pin.integrate instead of direct per-element differentiation for finite difference validation.
translations.details.environments.0: Pinocchio C++ getFrameJacobian and floating base system; the original post does not specify Pinocchio version, robot model, or operating system.
translations.details.limits.0: The original thread did not provide the corrected curve, Pinocchio version, or numerical error.
translations.details.limits.1: The original graph lacks a legend, axis names, and units, making it impossible to identify each color's speed component or calculation method from the graph.
translations.details.limits.2: The explanation of getFrameVelocity was corrected by the original reply; refer to the subsequent correction and current API documentation for the correct explanation.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author replied that the issue was resolved, and the alignment of coordinates yielded the expected result; the project contributor then closed the issue after the problem was resolved.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why is the Cartesian velocity from the LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED frame Jacobian not consistent with the numerical differentiation of the frame position?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before using the task space velocity feedback for the real machine, apply small perturbations, pin.integrate, and visualization to verify the coordinate expression of the base twist.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The original author confirmed that their floating base velocity, quaternion propagation, and integrator were processed in global coordinates, which is incompatible with the free-flyer local velocity provided by Pinocchio.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The blue solid line and purple dashed line in the first graph of the original post are clearly separated in multiple intervals.
translations.details.symptoms.1: In the second graph, the real and dashed lines for most qdot are nearly coincident, indicating that not all numerical differentiation failed.
translations.media_summaries.0: In the first graph of the original post, a group of blue solid lines and purple dashed lines shows deviation at peaks and at the end; shallow blue dashed lines and orange solid lines are clearly separated in the range of 20–60 on the x-axis; red and green zero-value lines coincide. No legend, axis name, or unit is present, so only the original author's statement about the speed mismatch can be confirmed, and no specific component can be inferred from the color.
translations.media_summaries.1: In the second graph of the original post, the real and dashed lines for non-zero components are nearly coincident in most x-axis ranges, and the zero-value lines also coincide; this aligns with the text in the original post 'some qdot and diff(q) are consistent with expectations.' Since there is no legend, axis name, or unit, it is not possible to confirm the physical components that cannot be identified from the graph.
